result.topic_en: Diary entries from 1812–1814 recording the recovery of a proof of the fundamental theorem of algebra, a new theory of the attraction of an elliptic spheroid, the discovery of the foundation of the general theory of biquadratic residues, and an inductive observation linking biquadratic residues to lemniscatic functions.
result.transcription:
Catalogum praecedentem per fata iniqua iterum interruptum
initio anni 1812 resumimus. In mense Nov. 1811 contigerat
demonstrationem theorematis fundamentalis in doctrina aequa-
tionum pure analyticam completam reddere; sed quum nihil
chartis servatum fuerit, pars quaedam {+essentialis+} memoriae penitus
exciderat. Hanc per satis longum temporis intervallum
frustra quaesitam tandem feliciter redinvenimus 1812 febr. 29
Theoriam Attractionis Sphaeroidis Elliptici in puncta
extra solidum sita prorsus novam invenimus
Seeberg. 1812. Sept. 26
Etiam partes reliquas eiusdem theoriae per methodum
novam mirae simplicitatis absolvimus 1812 Oct. 15 Gott:
Fundamentum theoriae residuorum biquadraticorum [-pro-]
{+generalis+}, per septem propemodum annos summa con-
tentione sed semper frustra quaesitum tandem feliciter dete-
ximus eodem die quo filius nobis natus est. 1813 Oct. 23 Gott.
Subtilissimum hoc est omnium eorum quae umquam
perfecimus. Vix itaque operae pretium est, his intermiscere
mentionem quarundam simplificationum ad calculum
orbitarum parabolicarum pertinentium.
Observatio per inductionem facta gravissima theoriam residuorum biquadra-
ticorum cum functionibus lemniscaticis elegantissime nectens. Puta si $a+bi$ est
numerus primus $a-1+bi$ per $2+2i$ divisibilis, multitudo omnium solutionum
congruentiae $1 = xx+yy+xxyy \pmod{a+bi}$, inclusis $x=\infty, y=\pm i$,
$x=\pm i, y=\infty$ fit $=(a-1)^2+bb$
1814 Jul 9.

quarundam simplificationum ad calculum

methods.what: Count of solutions of the lemniscatic congruence modulo a Gaussian prime a+bi with a-1+bi divisible by 2+2i, including points at infinity
methods.quote:
multitudo omnium solutionum
congruentiae $1 = xx+yy+xxyy \pmod{a+bi}$, inclusis $x=\infty, y=\pm i$,
$x=\pm i, y=\infty$ fit $=(a-1)^2+bb$

items.quote:
Observatio per inductionem facta gravissima theoriam residuorum biquadra-
ticorum cum functionibus lemniscaticis elegantissime nectens. Puta si $a+bi$ est
numerus primus $a-1+bi$ per $2+2i$ divisibilis, multitudo omnium solutionum
congruentiae $1 = xx+yy+xxyy \pmod{a+bi}$, inclusis $x=\infty, y=\pm i$,
$x=\pm i, y=\infty$ fit $=(a-1)^2+bb$
items.english: A most important observation made by induction, connecting the theory of biquadratic residues most elegantly with lemniscatic functions. Namely, if a+bi is a prime number and a-1+bi is divisible by 2+2i, the number of all solutions of the congruence 1 = xx+yy+xxyy (mod a+bi), including x=∞, y=±i and x=±i, y=∞, equals (a-1)^2+bb.

items.quote:
Subtilissimum hoc est omnium eorum quae umquam
perfecimus.
items.english: This is the most subtle of all the things we have ever accomplished.
